name: SG90 360° continuous-rotation micro servo
description: 9 g SG90-size micro servo modified for continuous 360° rotation: there is no end stop and no position feedback, so the 50 Hz control pulse sets speed and direction instead of angle (about 1.5 ms = stop, 1.0 ms = full speed clockwise, 2.0 ms = full speed anticlockwise). About 110–120 RPM at 4.8–5 V, 1.3–1.7 kgf·cm stall torque, 4.8–6 V supply, 110–250 mA moving and up to 300 mA stalled. Sold as: ProtoSupplies Servo Motor Micro SG90 360 Degree Continuous Rotation, a bare servo with a 25 cm 3-wire lead and female 2.54 mm JR/Futaba plug (brown GND, red 5V, orange PWM signal), with horns and screws.
eli5: A tiny motor that keeps spinning: your board's pulse picks which way it turns and how fast, or makes it stop.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Brown wire: ground (join it to the microcontroller's GND)

pins.name: V+
pins.description: Red wire: servo supply 4.8–6 V (5 V typical); 110–250 mA moving, up to 300 mA stalled

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: Orange wire: control pulses, 50 Hz; 1.5 ms = stop, shorter = clockwise, longer = anticlockwise (3.3 V logic works)

supplierQuery: SG90 360 degree continuous rotation micro servo
buildNotes: Wire colours: brown = GND, red = V+ (4.8–6 V, 5 V typical), orange = PWM signal. A 3.3 V signal from an ESP32 or Pico drives it fine.
Power it from 5 V (a separate 5 V supply, or VIN/VBUS for a single servo), never from the 3.3 V pin, and join the supply ground to the board's GND.

The pulse sets speed, not angle: about 1500 µs stops it, 1000 µs is full speed clockwise and 2000 µs full speed anticlockwise. The exact stop point differs per unit (ProtoSupplies saw a stop zone of roughly 1420–1580 µs), so trim stop_us if it creeps at 'stop'.
Direction labels follow the Smarthon SG90 360 table; some clones turn the other way, so check yours with a short test first.
To stop it fully and save power, call off() to stop sending pulses. Add a 470 µF capacitor across V+ and GND if the board resets when the motor starts.
It looks identical to the normal 180° SG90 (often only a '360' sticker differs): angle code will just make this one spin.

driver.code:
# SG90 360-degree continuous-rotation micro servo, MicroPython driver.
# Standard RC servo signal: one positive pulse every 20 ms (50 Hz).
# On the continuous version the pulse sets SPEED and DIRECTION, not angle:
#   ~1500 us = stop (the stop point varies a little per unit: trim stop_us),
#   1000 us  = full speed clockwise, 2000 us = full speed anticlockwise
#   (Smarthon SG90 360 table; some clones run the other way - test yours).
# ProtoSupplies measured the stop zone as roughly 1420-1580 us.
# Supply 4.8-6 V (5 V typical); a 3.3 V signal from an ESP32 / Pico works.
from machine import Pin, PWM

PERIOD_US = 20000  # 50 Hz frame


class SG90_360:
    def __init__(self, pin, stop_us=1500, span_us=500):
        self.stop_us = stop_us   # pulse that stops the motor (calibrate per unit)
        self.span_us = span_us   # stop_us +/- span_us = full speed
        self.pwm = PWM(pin if isinstance(pin, Pin) else Pin(pin), freq=50)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)     # no pulses: motor idle

    def write_us(self, us):
        us = max(self.stop_us - self.span_us, min(self.stop_us + self.span_us, us))
        self.pwm.duty_u16(int(us * 65535 // PERIOD_US))

    def speed(self, pct):
        """pct -100..100: negative = clockwise, positive = anticlockwise, 0 = stop."""
        pct = max(-100, min(100, pct))
        self.write_us(self.stop_us + self.span_us * pct / 100)

    def stop(self):
        self.write_us(self.stop_us)

    def off(self):
        """Stop sending pulses: the motor stops and the servo idles (about 10 mA)."""
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)

    def deinit(self):
        self.pwm.deinit()

example.code:
import time
from sg90_360 import SG90_360

servo = SG90_360({PWM})
servo.stop()
print('stop')
time.sleep(1.5)
servo.speed(-100)
print('clockwise')
time.sleep(2)
servo.speed(100)
print('anticlockwise')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
